load_bearing_verifications.claim: The current US letrozole, anastrozole, and exemestane labels and their embedded controlled-safety tables contain no gout, hyperuricemia, uric-acid, serum-urate, or blood-uric term.
A randomized male letrozole trial demonstrated increased testosterone and decreased estradiol but did not report a serum-urate or renal-urate-handling endpoint.
The direct head-to-head FATA-GIM3 trial reported no unexpected serious adverse events, while urate was not a reported endpoint in its publication abstract.
Published letrozole and anastrozole hyperuricemia reports include acute tumor lysis syndrome after endocrine therapy in advanced breast cancer.
The published palbociclib-letrozole hyperuricemia cases attributed management to palbociclib interruption and dose reduction.
The 12 source FAERS reports resolve to 10 deduplicated cases; only one report lists letrozole as the sole suspect, and it lacks event chronology.

limitations: FAERS lacks a denominator and the available fields do not establish incidence or causality; duplicate manufacturer reports and incomplete chronology required case-level interpretation.
The randomized-safety and landmark-trial PubMed snapshots were capped at 50 records and are marked partial.
No claim of universal literature absence was made; the direct-endpoint statement is bounded to the sources and search frames recorded here.
CQVIP and J-STAGE broad term matching prevented exact paired-query counts, and WanFang exposed no static result set.
No non-English source supplied a load-bearing claim, so the two-model translation protocol was not triggered.
